parts.latex:
The basal metabolic rate (BMR) of a person refers to the minimum amount of energy (in kilojoules) needed to sustain basic bodily functions (that is, to keep the person alive) for a 24-hour period.

The Harris-Benedict Model can be used to estimate BMR, in kJ/day. It is given by:

$$\text{BMR}_{\text{female}} = 2783 + 40.0W + 7.7H - 19.6A$$

where $W$ is weight (in kg), $H$ is height (in cm) and $A$ is age (in years)

A 20-year old woman weighs 60 kg and she has a height of 157 cm. Use the Harris-Benedict Model to estimate the woman's BMR.

Give your answer to the nearest kJ/day

figures.cap: graph of line AD with points B(50,150) and C

parts.latex: Find the equation of the line $AD$.
Explain why this line is only relevant between $B$ and $C$ for this factory.

The profit per week, \$$P$, can be found by using the equation $P = 24x + 15y$.

Compare the profits at $B$ and $C$.

solutions.latex:
The line $AD$ joins the points where boots plus sandals total 200.
$$\begin{aligned} x + y &= 200 \\ y &= -x + 200 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex: The maximum number of boots is $120$, so $x$ cannot be greater than $120$.

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
At $B$, $x = 50$ and $y = 150$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 24 \times 50 + 15 \times 150 \\ &= \$3450 \end{aligned}$$
At $C$, $x = 120$ and $y = 80$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 24 \times 120 + 15 \times 80 \\ &= \$4080 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore at $C$ the profit is $\$630$ more than at $B$.
criteria: Correctly finds one of the profits, or equivalent merit

7764.stem:
Wind turbines, such as those shown, are used to generate power.

\exfigure{1228_q13_1}

In theory, the power that could be generated by a wind turbine is modelled using the equation

$$T = 20\,000w^3,$$

where

$T$ is the theoretical power generated, in watts

$w$ is the speed of the wind, in metres per second

figures.cap: graph of theoretical and actual power against wind speed

parts.latex: Using this equation, what is the theoretical power generated by a wind turbine if the wind speed is $7.3$ m/s?

In practice, the actual power generated by a wind turbine is only 40% of the theoretical power.

If $A$ is the actual power generated, in watts, write an equation for $A$ in terms of $w$.

A particular farm requires at least 4.4 million watts of actual power in order to be self-sufficient.

What is the minimum wind speed required for the farm to be self-sufficient?
parts.note: Solving 8000w^3 = 4.4 million needs a cube root, which is rearranging beyond linear and y = ax^2 + c.

parts.latex:
A more accurate formula to calculate the power ($P$) generated by a wind turbine is

$$P = 0.61 \times \pi \times r^2 \times w^3,$$

where

$r$ is the length of each blade, in metres

$w$ is the speed of the wind, in metres per second

Each blade of a particular wind turbine has a length of 43 metres. The turbine operates at a wind speed of 8 m/s.

Using the formula above, if the wind speed increased by 10%, what would be the percentage increase in the power generated by this wind turbine?

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The actual power is $40\%$ of the theoretical power.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 0.4 \times 20\,000w^3 \\ &= 8000w^3 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
From the graph at $w = 9$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 5.8 \text{ million watts} \\ T &= 14.6 \text{ million watts} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Difference} &= 14.6 - 5.8 \\ &= 8.8 \text{ million watts} \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, calculate from the formulas at $w = 9$.
$$\begin{aligned} T &= 20\,000 \times 9^3 = 14\,580\,000 \text{ watts} \\ A &= 8000 \times 9^3 = 5\,832\,000 \text{ watts} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Difference} &= 14\,580\,000 - 5\,832\,000 \\ &= 8\,748\,000 \text{ watts} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds one of $A$ or $T$ correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Graph reading $8.8$ million is consistent with the calculated $8.748$ million.

solutions.latex:
The farm needs $A = 4\,400\,000$ watts.
$$\begin{aligned} 8000w^3 &= 4\,400\,000 \\ w^3 &= 550 \\ w &= 8.1932\ldots \\ &\approx 8.2 \text{ m/s (1 dp)} \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Use $r = 43$ and $w = 8$ in $P = 0.61 \times \pi \times r^2 \times w^3$.
$$P = 0.61 \times \pi \times 43^2 \times 8^3 = 1\,814\,205.92 \text{ watts}$$
A $10\%$ increase in speed gives
$$w = 8 \times 110\% = 8.8 \text{ m/s}$$
$$P = 0.61 \times \pi \times 43^2 \times 8.8^3 = 2\,414\,708.08 \text{ watts}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Increase} &= 2\,414\,708.08 - 1\,814\,205.92 \\ &= 600\,502.16 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage increase} &= \dfrac{600\,502.16}{1\,814\,205.92} \times 100\% \\ &\approx 33\% \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds both powers, or equivalent merit
Finds one power correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source wrote $0.331 \approx 33\%$; shown as the percentage. Power values differ slightly in the last digits from a calculator but the result is unchanged.

parts.latex:
The hiring charge, \$$C$, for a bobcat is determined by the formula:

$$C = 1385d + 850$$

where $d$ is the number of days the bobcat is hired, irrespective of the number of hours that the bobcat is used on any day. What is the total cost of hiring a bobcat for 17 days and 7 hours?

solutions.latex:
The bobcat is charged per day irrespective of hours, so $17$ days and $7$ hours is charged as $18$ days.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= 1385 \times 18 + 850 \\ &= \$25\,780 \end{aligned}$$
This matches option D.
